newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends lower, securities inactive.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends lower, securities inactive.

text.p: Indian call money ended marginally lower on Tuesday at 7.25 percent against the day's opening levels of 8.0-8.5 percent, dealers said.
They said demand from foreign and private banks kept the rates firm in the morning, restricting the downward movement.
"Rates saw a downward trend towards the end of the day, as most banks have alreay covered ahead of the reporting Friday," said a dealer at private mutual fund.

"One of the financial institutions has done a repos transaction for 25 billion rupees," he said. "These funds will go out of the system on Saturday, and the outflow could push rates up to 10 percent next week."
Another dealer said a 20 billion rupee securities auction on December 23 by the Reserve Bank of India could also put pressure on call money rates.
"As funds flow out, there will be some pressure on rates," he said.
The securities market was largely inactive on Tuesday, with some demand for 91-day treasury bills, said Chandra Shetty, dealer at Mata Securities.
"Volume was not so large, it slipped to 605 million rupees compared to yesterday's 720 million rupees," Shetty said.
Treasury bills maturing in February were traded at a yield of 8.95 percent, while January treasury bills yielded 8.74 percent, dealers said.
There were no trades in commercial paper and certificates of deposit, Shetty added.
